part_title: Amazon Managed Grafana: Observability Data Sources, Dashboards and Alerts

scenes.title: Amazon Managed Grafana Architecture
scenes.narration: This architecture separates the people viewing dashboards from the AWS services supplying telemetry. On the left, users authenticate to an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace through supported identity integrations, such as IAM Identity Center or a configured SAML provider. Within the workspace, Viewer, Editor and Admin roles control what the person can do. The workspace uses a different identity and permission boundary to query data sources such as CloudWatch, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, X-Ray and compatible third-party systems. Follow the source arrows into the dashboards: CPU utilisation, request rate, P-ninety-five latency and error counts are visualised in panels, with alerts configured for actionable conditions. The key security distinction is that signing into a workspace does not automatically grant access to every data source. Workspace role settings, data-source credentials, IAM permissions and query scope must all be considered. Grafana stores dashboards and configuration, but does not replace the underlying metrics, logs or trace stores. Build an observability design where authorised users can inspect the necessary evidence without exposing unrelated accounts or confidential telemetry.

scenes.title: Amazon Managed Grafana for GenAI Operations
scenes.narration: This dashboard shows how a GenAI operations team brings application, queue and infrastructure signals together. At the top, filters select the service, environment and time range; always confirm those selections before diagnosing a spike. The latency panel compares median response times with P-ninety-five performance, revealing whether a small portion of requests suffers much worse delays. Error and throttling trends distinguish failures in application logic from pressure on dependent APIs. Queue backlog shows whether asynchronous workers are falling behind, while CPU, memory and GPU charts help identify resource exhaustion. From the dashboard, an operator can investigate related logs and traces when those data sources are configured and accessible. An alert only reaches SNS, email or an incident tool when the routing and notification channels are explicitly set up. The bottom security notes matter: restrict IAM and data-source permissions, encrypt telemetry, and review plugin and feature compatibility for the workspace version. For model inference, combine technical measurements with request rate and quality metrics; low CPU alone does not prove there is no model or quota bottleneck.
